title: Another chat's labels are written without reading that chat
body:
**Rule** (set by the maintainer): a chat's memory or labels may be changed from outside that chat only after the model has read the chat itself (its source) and found them wrong or missing.

**Problem**
The sorting call added in v0.15.0 (#96) gives chats indexed before 0.14/0.15 a subject, type and project in one call per workspace, from each chat's one-line summary and topic labels only. The model never reads those chats, so a label can be a guess about a conversation it has not seen.

Everything else already keeps the rule: a chat's index writes only that chat's own topics, links and labels, from its own messages; matching and recall only read other chats; hiding and deleting are the user's own actions.

**Fix**
- Each older chat is labelled by a call of its own that reads that chat: its kept messages (#93), cut to the indexing input cap as indexing cuts a span, with its summary and the workspace's subjects to reuse.
- Only labels the chat lacks are filled; labels its own index named are never replaced from outside.
- A chat whose messages cannot be read (nothing kept) is left unlabelled rather than guessed.
- At most 10 chats per workspace per app run, so an upgrade does not spend everything at once.

title: A chat does not know which memory branch it is
body:
**Rule** (set by the maintainer): a chat knows what it is in memory; chat 7 is c7 in the tree.

**Problem**
The user sees `c7` in the header (#92) and in Memory tree, but the model in that chat is never told. Its notes name other chats (`c3n12`), the chat list leaves it out, and when the user says "c7" or asks what this chat is in memory, the model cannot tell.

**Fix**
- With the first memory note a chat gets once it has a number, one line: `This chat is c7 in memory` and how its own turns are read (`recall("t3")`); again only when no note of the plugin is left in the chat (after a compaction). About 20 tokens, once.
- `/context-graph` (stats) says which chat this is.
- `recall("c7t3")` in chat 7 reads its own turn, like `recall("t3")`.

title: Savings: count the conversation history memory stands in for, minus what memory costs
body:
**Rule** (set by the maintainer): a chat never takes earlier chats in as input; it uses their memory tree and digs into deeper layers only when needed. Tokens saved = the old total (the earlier conversation history that would otherwise have been input) - the tokens used for memory making and searching.

**Problem**
The first part holds already: other chats reach the model only as topic lines, and sources and turns only by recall. The estimate does not follow the rule: it counts, for each topic used, only its three newest messages as stored, so it measures what one paste of a few messages would have cost, not the history memory replaces.

**Fix**
- Old total: for each earlier chat whose memory a chat actually used (a recall, or an answer saying two of a topic's words the prompt did not), that chat's whole kept conversation (#93), in tokens, counted once per chat that used it, at the time of the first use.
- Memory making: the indexing calls (as dsh reported them; cached input x0.1, output x4).
- Searching: the notes and recalls sent, their cached re-sends (x0.1) and the recall tool (x0.1).
- Saved = old total - making - searching, shown with each term on the card and the plugin's page. Ledgers written before are converted once, from the topics they recorded as used.

**Not changed, on purpose**: a chat's own history stays as dsh sends it. Folding it into the tree (tried in v0.2) breaks the provider's prompt cache, which bills repeated input at about a tenth of the price, so it costs more than it saves; dsh's own compaction handles long chats.
